  "important_episodes_or_facts_lost": [
    "The 2004 videoescandalo narrative (Units 22-23) preserves the actors (Ponce, Bejarano, Imaz, Ahumada, Döring, Rosario Robles, Leonel Godoy) but loses the specific content of the 'compromising situations' (Las Vegas casino roulette, cash bundles, political favors with Ahumada) only in summary form, though the original is cited.",
    "The November 2004 Tláhuac lynching episode (Unit 25) — President Fox removed Marcelo Ebrard as Mexico City security secretary; López Obrador protested and retained Ebrard by appointing him social-development secretary. The paper captures this but loses the specificity of the trigger event (three federal police agents lynched) and the dual dismissal (Ebrard plus the PFP commissioner).",
    "The 2008 'Consulta energética' (Unit 40) — one million citizens participated; the paper reports this figure and the National Movement in Defense of Petroleum but loses the specific legislative outcome (seven decree-laws, creation of the Comisión Nacional de Hidrocarburos, renegotiated exploitation contracts approved in October 2008 with PRI/PAN/PVEM plus 'Los Chuchos' PRD votes).",
    "The 2010 gas import figure (Unit 42) — Mexico imported 40% of consumed gasoline; combined with declining oil production under Calderón. The paper preserves this but loses the specific 'terrible crisis' framing and the proposed remedy (major investments in exploration and refining).",
    "The 2012 formal challenge (Unit 50) — 639-page legal document plus 49-page annex alleging purchase of five million votes and excessive campaign spending in violation of Article 41. The paper mentions the 639-page submission but loses the specific Annex 49-page detail and the constitutional Article 41 reference.",
    "The 2006 election narrow margin sequence (Units 33-35) — PREP gave Calderón 36.38% vs. López Obrador 35.34% (1.04% gap at 98.4% count); final district count gave 35.89% vs. 35.31% (0.58% gap = 243,934 votes); partial recount in 11,839 polling stations (9% of total) in 149 districts in 26 states annulled 237,000 votes (Calderón lost 81,000, AMLO lost 77,000); final margin 0.56% (233,831 votes). The paper mentions the 0.56% final and 11,839 stations but loses the complete sequential tabulation and the proportionality of vote annulment.",
    "The 2017 Estado de México gubernatorial result (Unit 57) — Delfina Gómez Álvarez (MORENA) at 33.6% against Alfredo del Mazo Maza (PRI/PVEM/PANAL/PES), described as the lowest percentage in PRI history in the state. The paper does not surface this specific empirical anchor for AMLO's 2018 momentum.",
    "The PRD internal schism and MORENA's 2015 debut (Unit 55) — MORENA: 8.8% national vote, 35 deputies; PRD: 11.4% and 56; PAN 108, PRI 203; in DF, MORENA 20 of 66 assembly deputies vs. PRD 17, plus 5 of 16 delegaciones vs. PRD 6. The paper omits these specific vote shares and seat counts.",
    "The 2018 coalition arithmetic (Unit 66) — Juntos Haremos Historia: 308/500 deputies, 69/128 senators; gubernaturas won (CDMX/Sheinbaum, Chiapas/Escandón, Tabasco/Adán Augusto López, Veracruz/Cuitláhuac García, Morelos/Cuauhtémoc Blanco via PES); MORENA first in 18 of 27 state congresses. The paper captures the congressional majorities but loses state-level specifics and the 5 gubernatorial wins.",
    "The 2008 PRD internal election annulment (Unit 41) — 16 March 2008 internal CEN election, Encinas vs. Ortega; Commission annulled on 19 July 2008; TEPJF overturned on 12 November 2008; Ortega took office 29 November 2008. The paper does not treat this intra-party governance episode.",
    "The 2012 Movimiento Progresista congressional performance (Unit 51) — 135 deputies (second bloc after PRI-PVEM), 28 of 128 senators; gubernatorial gains (Morelos with Graco Ramírez-Garrido Abreu, Tabasco with Arturo Núñez Jiménez) and losses (Chiapas); DF figures (AMLO 52.9% presidential, Mancera 63.6% gubernatorial, 14 of 16 delegaciones, 40 of 66 local deputies). The paper omits these.",
    "The FOBAPROA narrative (Unit 17) — post-December 1994 financial crisis, the fund converted private banker losses into public debt; López Obrador's book 'Fobaproa, expediente abierto: reseña y archivo' characterized it as unconstitutional and 'the greatest fraud after the Conquest.' The paper preserves the characterization but loses the specific post-1994-crisis causal chain and the book-title detail.",
    "The 2018 Project Alternativo de Nación structure (Unit 60) — coordinated by Alfonso Romo Garza; four commissions (Economy and Development, Social Development, Politics and Government, Education/Values/Culture/Science); seven lineamientos (Legalidad y erradicación de la corrupción; Combate a la pobreza; Recuperación de la paz; Viabilidad financiera y austeridad; Equidad de género; Desarrollo sostenible y buen vivir; Reconstrucción nacional). The paper retains Romo Garza and the seven-lineamiento list but loses the four-commission structure.",
    "The proposed 2012 cabinet (Unit 49) — Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas for Pemex, Marcelo Ebrard for Secretaría de Gobernación, Elena Poniatowska for Secretaría de Cultura. The paper lists these but omits the campaign context ('cambio tranquilo' messaging, the policlasista gestures).",
    "The 2012 electoral result and challenge (Units 49-50) — IFE rapid count gave Peña Nieto 37.93%-38.55%, AMLO 31%+; final cómputo 8 July: EPN 38.2%, AMLO 31.57%, gap of 3.3 million votes; TEPJF 30 August unanimously rejected the 639-page plus 49-page annex challenge as 'infundados' and 'jurídicamente improcedente.' The paper captures the broad outlines but loses the IFE rapid-count range and the unanimous TEPJF rejection language.",
    "The 2005 desafuero sequence (Units 25-27) — 7 April 2005 Cámara de Diputados voted 360-127-2 to lift immunity (PAN+PRI in favor, PRD+PT+Convergencia against, half PVEM and some PRI against); PGR unable to file charges; 25 April López Obrador returned to office; 27 April Fox accepted PGR Macedo de la Concha's resignation; 4 May new fiscal Cabeza de Vaca withdrew charges; settlement meeting at Los Pinos. The paper does not capture this chronology.",
    "The 2006 Convención Nacional Democrática and parallel government (Unit 36) — 16 September 2006, 'more than a million' (organizers) in Zócalo acclaimed López Obrador as 'legitimate president'; 20 November 2006 inauguration; 12 'secretarios' in the parallel cabinet; PRD deputies took Congressional tribune on 1 September 2006 to prevent Fox's final address. The paper does not preserve this.",
    "The energy reform 2008 specifics (Unit 41) — seven decree-laws; creation of the Comisión Nacional de Hidrocarburos; renegotiated exploitation contracts; October 2008 passage with PRI/PAN/PVEM votes plus 'Los Chuchos' PRD faction; PRD's resultant 2009 legislative collapse to 12.2% and 72 deputies (loss of 54). The paper mentions the 2008 passage but loses the 2009 electoral cost.",
    "Calderón's sexenio mortality figure (Unit 58) — 200,000 assassinated since 2006 plus thousands missing or displaced. The paper does not surface this empirical anchor.",
    "The López Obrador 2013 health episode (Unit 54) — December 2013 acute myocardial infarction requiring surgical intervention, survived. The paper does not include this biographical detail, which is immaterial to 5B questions.",
    "The FOBAPROA original purpose (Unit 17) — Fondo Bancario de Protección al Ahorro, created under Salinas to help depositors in bank insolvencies; post-1994 crisis converted liabilities of prominent bankers and businessmen into public debt. The paper captures the conversion but loses the original depositor-protection purpose.",
    "The 2008 MORENA opposition building (Unit 44) — 2 October 2011 formalized as civil association; 2,000+ sectional and municipal committees; December 2013 PRD break; 9 July 2014 INE registration as political party. The paper does not capture this chronology.",
    "The 2015 MORENA-PRI split in Estado de México (Unit 43) — April 2011 PRD national council rejected PAN alliance; López Obrador's February 2011 'licencia temporal' from PRD; Yeidckol Polevnsky as alternative candidate. The paper does not treat this.",
    "The Morena 2015 congressional debut (Unit 55) — 35 deputies nationwide; 20 of 66 DF assembly seats; 5 of 16 delegaciones. The paper does not preserve these specifics.",
    "The 2012 Movimiento Progresista loss of Chiapas gubernatorial (Unit 51) — PRD lost Chiapas to PRI but gained Morelos (Graco Ramírez-Garrido Abreu) and Tabasco (Arturo Núñez Jiménez). The paper does not capture this.",
    "The 2018 coalition formation sequence (Unit 59) — June 2017 MORENA III Congress; January 2018 Marcelo Ebrard joined MORENA; IV Congress 20 November 2017 presented the Proyecto; alliance only with PT (Alejandra Barrales/Mancera PRD offer rejected). The paper mentions the broad coalition context but loses the Ebrard 2018 recruitment and the explicit rejection of PRD/PRI/PAN/PVEM/PANAL/PES/MC alliances.",
    "The 2018 voto anticipado and disputed irregularities (Unit 64) — López Obrador opened campaign 1 April 2018 in Ciudad Juárez; closed 27 June 2018 at Estadio Azteca (87,000 capacity); Trump tweet congratulations; Anaya second at 22.27%, Meade 16.40%, Rodríguez Calderón 5.23%; AMLO first in all states except Guanajuato. The paper captures the vote shares but loses the campaign closing venue and the single-state exception.",
    "The 2018 USMCA framing (Unit 7) — López Obrador considered the USMCA 'beneficial'; October 2018 visas for migrants offer; 26 November 2018 Trump tear-gas incident and threat to permanently close the border. The paper preserves the USMCA characterization but loses the Trump-asylum-threat narrative.",
    "The 2008 AMLO book (Unit 40) — 'La gran tentación: el petróleo de México' (September 2008, his ninth book); presented arguments against the Calderón energy reform. The paper does not include this title detail.",
    "The 2012 PRD expulsion of López Obrador context (Unit 52) — September 2012, after TEPJF ruling, López Obrador announced MORENA's conversion to political party; 20 November 2012 Congress approved three basic documents; Martí Batres Guadarrama as CEN president; Bertha Elena Luján Uranga as secretary general; Consejo Nacional of 204 members including Paco Ignacio Taibo II, Rosario Ibarra de Piedra, René Drucker Colín, Claudia Sheinbaum, José Agustín Ortiz Pinchetti. The paper does not preserve this organizational detail.",
    "The 2018 MORENA pre-candidate registration (Unit 61) — 12 December 2017 pre-candidate registration; CEN presidency passed to Yeidckol Polevnsky; AMLO at 30% in polls; 16 March 2018 INE registration as coalition candidate; 'Cuarta Transformación' framework. The paper does not preserve the pre-candidate vs. candidate registration chronology."
  ],
  "fact_fidelity_notes": "Factual fidelity is generally high — specific figures (53.19%, 64.4% turnout, 308/500 deputies, 69/128 senators, 100 billion pesos first-year savings claim, 0.56% electoral margin, 11,839 polling stations, 9/26 partial recount coverage, 1.2 million jobs/year, 6% growth target, 171 pesos minimum wage by end of term, 1,500 pesos monthly pensions, 233,831 vote margin, 40% gasoline import share, 8.8% MORENA 2015 vote share, 35 deputies, 22.27% / 16.40% / 5.23% 2018 runner-up votes) are preserved correctly. The paper is faithful to the source's content and does not invent claims. The paper correctly identifies that the source provides no direct 2022 evidence and frames its content as pre-presidential antecedent material.",
  "omission_judgment": "The paper is an American Political Science Association-style structured evidence map with question-by-question coverage. It preserves the high-level commitments and the major pre-presidential episodes (videoescándalo, desafuero, FOBAPROA, energy reform battles, electoral disputes, Mexico City administration record). However, for a Chapter 5B judge assessing economic governance quality, the paper is too thin in several material areas: (1) the specific 2006 vote-count sequence and procedural details — relevant to 5B.7 (receptiveness to independent evaluation); (2) the precise 100-billion-peso savings claim and how it squares with Mexico City debt accumulation — relevant to 5B.3; (3) the 2018 MORENA coalition vote shares and the 2015 MORENA debut results — relevant to judge calibration of the electoral mandate that AMLO carried into December 2018; (4) the energy reform 2008 legislative arithmetic and the 2012 challenge's 639-page plus 49-page annex detail — relevant to 5B.5; (5) the FOBAPROA post-1994 causal chain — relevant to 5B.5; (6) the 2018 gubernatorial results (Sheinbaum CDMX, Escandón Chiapas, Adán Augusto López Tabasco, Cuitláhuac García Veracruz, Cuauhtémoc Blanco Morelos) — relevant to 5B.6 federalism context. The paper's strongest sections are the question-by-question evidence maps (Section 11), which assemble the source material into the required question framework. The paper's weakest section is Section 7 (corruption), which provides solid coverage of the videoescándalo but omits the 2012 FOBAPROA-specific commitment and the López Obrador book 'Fobaproa, expediente abierto: reseña y archivo' (Unit 17). The paper's Section 8 (transparency/audit) is well-developed but loses the 2017 PRD maneuverings and the 2018 fiscal-reserve flows. The paper's Section 9 (shock management) is appropriately brief because the source genuinely lacks target-year evidence. The paper's Section 10 (trajectory) is appropriately limited because the source predates the presidency. The paper's Section 11 question-by-question evidence maps are well-organized and faithful to the source, but each map is necessarily high-level and would benefit from more granular episode detail. The paper does not abstract or back-cover summarize; it provides structured argumentation. However, the loss of specific numeric anchors (electoral margins, vote shares, debt figures, energy import shares, congressional seat counts) limits a judge's ability to reason about the strength of mandates, the credibility of stated commitments, and the precedent for accepting or rejecting unfavorable institutional findings.",
  "additional_notes": "The source (CIDOB) is a pre-presidential political biography published 29 November 2018 with narrative coverage through 6 August 2018 and a single administrative update noting the end of López Obrador's presidency on 1 October 2024. The source's epistemic limitation is intrinsic and substantial: it provides no 2022 target-year evidence. The paper correctly identifies this and structures its content as pre-presidential antecedent. The paper is not an abstract or back-cover summary; it preserves the source's specific episodes (videoescándalo, desafuero, 2008 energy consulta, FOBAPROA, 2012 challenge, 2006 election dispute, Mexico City administration record, 2018 coalition). The paper adequately explains what happened, not just what topics exist. However, the paper's question-by-question evidence maps (Section 11) function more as analytical summaries than as fact repositories; a judge would need to re-cross-reference the source's specific numeric claims to reason about the credibility of AMLO's stated commitments, the precedent for rejecting unfavorable institutional findings, and the strength of the mandate AMLO carried into December 2018. The paper's overall documentary contribution assessment (Section 12) is appropriately calibrated."
}
